content.text:
I'm trying to figure out how the grid is divided into objects—it looks like the 6x6 grid splits into 3x3 quadrant blocks, and I'm working out which quadrant gets colored based on some pattern rule.

Now I'm re-checking connectivity in the diagonal example: the anti-diagonal 8s form one connected component, and I'm tracing through the actual grid cell-by-cell to determine which cells belong together using diagonal adjacency, mapping out how r1, r2, r3, and r4 groups link into larger components.

Averaging row positions, the first small component (rows 0-1) gives about 0.4, the big merged component gives about 2.44, and the last component (rows 4-5) gives about 4.75 -- so the minimum-row component is the first one.

I'm mapping out the grid of 7s and tracing which cells connect into groups, starting to trace out the first connected component from the top-right corner.

Tracing the remaining components, I calculate their average row positions: component B centers around row 3.25, and component C (just two cells) centers at row 5. Since component A has the lowest average row position at 0.75, it's the target to recolor.
